clue.text: Amount of power in what one hears

indicators.note: what a listener hears is the sound of a word, not its spelling

parts.note: the question word said out loud matches the unit of power

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how much power is carried in the sound we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The watt is the SI unit measuring power, so it names an amount of it.

clue.text: Subtle changes in most intense colour

definitions.note: read as 'of the most intense colour', an adjective like the answer

indicators.note: the word subtle undergoes changes, so its letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter notices delicate variations in the deepest shade.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of blue describes something most strongly coloured blue, the deepest hue.

clue.text: Bunk in toolshed, oddly selected quarters

indicators.note: split the word into four equal parts and keep only the first and third, the odd-numbered quarters

parts.note: taken as written; its eight letters make four quarters of two

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping on a bunk in the garden shed, quartered there oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: The quarters are TO, OL, SH and ED; the odd ones, first and third, are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk and tosh are both informal British words for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Way in which royalty supports author

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: Thomas Mann, the German novelist
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: How a royal family props up a favoured writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner is a way or method of doing something, as in 'in this manner'.

clue.text: Part of exam that ends with appropriate mark

definitions.text: Part of exam that ends with appropriate mark

parts.note: surface reading: one section of a test
setter's reading: the punctuation mark named after this very item closes it, so the mark is fitting

explanation.surface: A section of a test that is graded with a fair score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' sounds like the score an examiner gives; it is really the punctuation mark that ends such a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is made of items each asking something, and a written one ends with its namesake punctuation mark.

clue.text: Losing some put in another form for new terms

indicators.note: letters put into another form are rearranged into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer rephrases familiar words and coins fresh vocabulary along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Neologisms are newly coined words or expressions entering the language.

clue.text: Bachelor with partner husband loves — what a commotion!

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor
an ally is a partner
H is the abbreviation for husband
love is a nil score in tennis, so two loves are two zeros, letter O

explanation.surface: A single man and his partner, with a husband and romance, cause a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss or uproar, the commotion the exclamation complains about.

clue.text: Monotonous rhymes for some

parts.note: a word rhyming with 'some'
another word that rhymes with 'some'

explanation.surface: A complaint that some verse is dull and plodding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhymes for some' asks for words rhyming with 'some': HUM and DRUM, which themselves make a rhyming compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum describes something dull and lacking variety, which is what monotonous means.

clue.text: I concur about copper's shrewdness

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it on both sides

parts.note: said to agree with a prayer or statement
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Agreeing that a policeman is sharp-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight and good judgement, the quality called shrewdness.

clue.text: Master mistreated group of pupils

indicators.note: something mistreated is knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster has treated a class badly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a stream is a set of pupils grouped by ability.

clue.text: Wren's building is in sacred setting, I assure you!

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it
a setting surrounds what sits in it, like a mount around a gem

parts.note: holy means sacred
what a wren, the small bird, builds

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a Christopher Wren church stands in holy surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Wren looks like the architect Sir Christopher Wren, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Honestly!' is an interjection used to insist on one's truthfulness, like 'I assure you'.

clue.text: Business dependent on intensive stock control

definitions.text: Business dependent on intensive stock control

parts.note: surface reading: rigorous management of a firm's inventory
setter's reading: an agricultural enterprise that keeps livestock confined and intensively managed

explanation.surface: A company whose success relies on tight inventory management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' reads as goods in a warehouse, but it means farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: This agricultural practice raises livestock at high density indoors, an intensive system controlling the animals closely.

clue.text: Money-grubbing article, full of malice about a king

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: the word about here means being placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: vicious means full of malice
A taken as written, plus R for rex, king

explanation.surface: A greedy newspaper piece, spiteful in its treatment of a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The malicious word goes about A and R, which sit after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaricious means greedy for wealth, which is what money-grubbing describes.

clue.text: What's always coming after onset of flu?

definitions.text: What's always coming after onset of flu?

indicators.note: one piece coming after another is placed right behind it
the onset of something is its beginning, so take the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of flu
ever means always

explanation.surface: A question about what invariably follows the first signs of influenza.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a definition: a high temperature reliably follows the first signs of flu.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised body temperature is the classic symptom that follows soon after influenza takes hold.

clue.text: Starts off producing answers the hard way

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters, taken off them

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A solver reaches the solutions only by doing things the difficult way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard way' looks like an idiom; only 'way' is the definition, and 'the hard' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a route or track, a way from one place to another.

clue.text: Her pilot manoeuvred into place for landing aircraft

indicators.note: things manoeuvred are moved about, so these letters change position

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's pilot steered the aircraft into a spot to touch down.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliport is an airport for helicopters, a place where those craft land.

clue.text: Picture that is appended to second volume

indicators.note: something appended is attached at the end of what follows it in the clue

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
V is the abbreviation for volume
i.e., Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: An illustration has been added to the second book of a set.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British informal for a moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture is an informal word for a film, as in 'going to the pictures'.

clue.text: Each food provided is as it should be

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
the food a household provides, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: Every meal served meets the proper standard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: food that is as it should be can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Eatable means fit to be consumed, the condition food ought to be in.

clue.text: Affected by cold, one may run under bridge

definitions.text: Affected by cold, one may run under bridge

parts.note: surface reading: a river or stream flowing beneath a bridge
setter's reading: a facial feature that runs when you have a cold, sitting below the bony bridge

explanation.surface: A frozen river still flowing beneath a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' and 'bridge' suggest water under a crossing; the bridge is part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold makes this facial organ run, and its upper bony part is called the bridge.

clue.text: Poorly perform again in front of head, showing lack of education

indicators.note: a piece in front of another comes before it in the answer

parts.note: ill means poorly
to iterate is to repeat, do again
a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: Doing badly at a retake before the headteacher reveals poor schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher; it is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiterateness is the state of being unable to read or write, an absence of education.

clue.text: Supporter of monarch's behind cast in audition

indicators.note: an audition is literally a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: cast means thrown, and the past participle has the same sound

explanation.surface: An actor playing a king's backer was cast at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter of monarch's behind' looks like someone backing a ruler; it is what the ruler sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is the ceremonial chair on which a sovereign sits, so it literally holds up the royal rear.

clue.text: Fool making different points with it each time

parts.note: N, north, one compass point
taken as written
W, west, a different compass point
'it' again, added on the second occasion

explanation.surface: A fool makes a different argument every time he speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' sounds like arguments; they are two compass points, each followed by IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly or stupid person, an informal word for a fool.

clue.text: Occurs, as such, after middle of radio broadcast

indicators.note: the words before this come after the piece that follows it
the middle of a word is the letter at its centre

parts.note: the central letter of radio
something that occurs is, exists
per se, Latin for 'by itself, as such'

explanation.surface: Something happens, of its own kind, after the middle of a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like part of the radio picture; it is the verb meaning scatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, and disperse means to spread or scatter.

clue.text: Moderate repeatedly taking part in ceasefire, as expected

indicators.note: the letters are taking part in the words that follow, and they are found there twice over

parts.note: sits inside the word for a truce, and again across its last letter and the next two words

explanation.surface: Tension is eased repeatedly as both sides join a truce, just as predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters appear twice: within ceasefire itself, and spanning ceasefirE AS Expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to moderate or lessen something, such as pain or pressure.

clue.text: Soldier attending major film

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an officer's personal servant in the British Army
second meaning: a big-budget superhero movie

explanation.surface: A soldier present at a blockbuster screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' reads as an adjective for the film; it is the army rank being served.
explanation.definitionFit: A British officer's orderly is called this, and it is also the title of the comic-book hero's films.

clue.text: State requirement for sentence being cut

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: every grammatical sentence needs a verb

explanation.surface: Stating what is needed before a prisoner's sentence is reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' suggests a prison term; it is the grammatical sense. 'A verb' loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something firmly, to state it.

clue.text: Defeated in race? Without rancour, taking heart

indicators.note: taking away the part meaning heart removes it from the word

parts.note: out means outside, without
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner beaten without bitterness, keeping their spirits up.
explanation.walkthrough: COUR is removed: it echoes French cœur, heart, and begins courage, which is also called heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun someone is to beat them by running faster, so the past tense means defeated in a race.

clue.text: Detailed description one put before people, for example

indicators.note: items put before another come first in the answer

parts.note: short for specification
the Roman numeral for one
men, people

explanation.surface: Someone wants a full account written ahead of the people involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like a phrase introducing an instance; only 'example' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a single sample taken as representative, an example of its kind.
